title: Remove Comments
summary: Given a C++ program represented as an array of strings, where each string is a line of code, remove all comments.
statement: Given a C++ program represented as an array of strings, where each string is a line of code, remove all comments. Comments are of two types: line comments starting with // and block comments starting with /* and ending with */. Line comments extend to the end of the line, and block comments are ignored until the matching */ is found. The first comment found on a line takes precedence. Lines that become empty after comment removal are excluded. The input will not contain control characters, single quotes, or double quotes. Every open block comment will be properly closed, and implicit newline characters are removed by block comments. After removing the comments, return the source code in the same format.
constraints: Source contains valid // line comments and /* */ block comments; quoted strings are excluded.
Remove comments and omit empty output lines while joining code around multiline blocks.
hints: Line comments end at the current line; block comments preserve parser state across lines.
Scan characters while tracking whether a block is open and buffer surviving code.
Outside a block, // stops the line and /* opens a block; */ closes it; flush only outside blocks.
The state machine consumes every comment delimiter once and joins code fragments exactly when a block crosses lines.
editorial: The state machine consumes every comment delimiter once and joins code fragments exactly when a block crosses lines.

tests.explanation: Both comment forms disappear while surviving spaces and program lines remain in order.
Code on opposite sides of a multiline block joins into ab.
